body.justification: The full-data interval has exact finite-sample conditional coverage and the four-term upper expected-length rate for every compatible envelope.
body.gap: The matching four-channel expected-length converse requires \(B>D^2\); equality retains only the three proved non-donor lower channels.
body.consumer: Analysts obtain conditionally honest inference at every compatible relative-growth configuration without an overstated boundary donor converse.
body.proof_tex:
The compatibility calculation (1) in \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} shows that \(B<D^2\) gives an empty class.  Fix a compatible envelope \(B\ge D^2\), let
\[
\mathscr X=\sigma\{X_{st}:s\le S,\ t\le T\},
\]
and condition first on \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\).  On each successful fit, polynomial reproduction from \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control}, applied to the degree-\(r\) Taylor polynomial of \(m_s\) at \(\widetilde z_s\), gives
\[
\left|e_0^\top\widehat\gamma_s-m_s(\widetilde z_s)
-\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}\right|
\le C_{r,d}L\sum_{t=1}^{T}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}|a_{sti}|
\|X_{st}-\widetilde z_s\|_2^\lambda.
\tag{34}
\]
After cohort weighting, the right side is exactly \(A_L\).

Define the historical unit-cluster variables
\[
\mathsf H_{si}=\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}a_{sti}\varepsilon_{sti}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:historical-full-design-centering} and donor independence give
\[
\mathbb E_P[\mathsf H_{si}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]=0.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} makes these variables independent over \((s,i)\) under this conditioning.  Since \(0\le Q_{sti}\le B\), the conditional range length of \(\mathsf H_{si}\) is at most
\[
c_{si}=B\pi_s\sum_{t=1}^{T}|a_{sti}|.
\]
If a conditionally centered random variable \(U\) lies in an interval of length \(c\), convexity of \(x\mapsto e^{vx}\) bounds its exponential moment by the endpoint mixture with the same mean; differentiating the logarithm of that two-point mixture gives
\[
\mathbb E[e^{vU}\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)]\le e^{v^2c^2/8}.
\tag{35}
\]
Multiplying (35) over independent unit clusters, applying exponential Markov inequality, optimizing over \(v>0\), and repeating for \(-U\) yield
\[
P_P\left\{
\left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathsf H_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}.
\tag{36}
\]
Thus each unit's full calendar history is one bounded cluster; no within-unit temporal restriction is used.

Similarly define
\[
\mathsf E_{si}=\frac{\pi_s}{n_s}
\{B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}-\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid E_0]\}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:event-full-design-mean-stability} centers \(\mathsf E_{si}\) given \((\mathscr X,E_0)\); donor independence preserves centering after donors are adjoined, and cross-unit independence gives conditional independence.  Their conditional range lengths are at most \(B\pi_s/n_s\).  The same calculation gives
\[
P_P\left\{
\left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathsf E_{si}\right|>R_{\mathrm{evt}}
\,\middle|\,\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\right\}
\le\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}.
\tag{37}
\]
A union bound combines (36)--(37), without requiring independence between one unit's historical path and event outcome.

For donor calibration define only in this proof
\[
Y_j=\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0),
\qquad
W_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^{N}Y_j.
\]
The conditional fourth-moment expansion in (30) gives
\[
\mathbb E_P[\|W_N\|_2^4\mid E_0]
\le\frac BN+\left(1-\frac1N\right)(D^2+2D)=M_4(N).
\tag{38}
\]
Define the proof event \(\mathcal D_N=\{\|W_N\|_2\le q_N\}\).  Markov's inequality and the definition of \(q_N\) imply
\[
P_P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)
\le\frac{M_4(N)}{q_N^4}=\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{39}
\]
Projection onto \([0,1]^{Sd}\) cannot increase Euclidean distance from \(z_0\), because \(z_0\) lies in that cube.  The covariance eigenvalue bounds therefore give, on \(\mathcal D_N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z-z_0)\|_2
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\widetilde z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|\bar Z-z_0\|_2\\
&\le\sqrt{C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma}\,q_N/\sqrt N
=\delta_N.
\end{aligned}
\tag{40}
\]
On the good event of \texttt{def:honest-interval}, \(\delta_N\le\delta_0\).  The upper half of \texttt{ass:local-two-sided-modulus} and (40) imply
\[
\left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
\{m_s(\widetilde z_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
\le C_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta_N^\kappa=A_{\mathrm{don}}.
\tag{41}
\]

Let \(\mathcal G\) denote the selector-and-radius good event in \texttt{def:honest-interval}; it is measurable with respect to \((\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j))\).  On \(\mathcal G^c\), the fallback interval is \([-B,B]\).  Every potential-outcome contrast has conditional mean in \([-B,B]\), and the positive cohort weights sum to one, so \(\tau_n(z_0)\in[-B,B]\) deterministically.  On \(\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N\), \texttt{lem:identification-fwl}, (34), and (41) decompose the estimation error into the event fluctuation, historical fluctuation, and two terms bounded by \(A_L\) and \(A_{\mathrm{don}}\).  Thus noncoverage implies failure of (36) or (37).  Iterated conditioning gives, for every positive sample size,
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_P\{\tau_n(z_0)\notin C_\alpha\mid E_0\}
&\le P_P(\mathcal D_N^c\mid E_0)\\
&\quad+\mathbb E_P\!\left[
\mathbf1_{\mathcal G\cap\mathcal D_N}
P_P\{\text{historical failure or event failure}
\mid\mathscr X,E_0,(Z_j)\}
\,\middle|\,E_0\right]\\
&\le\alpha_{\mathrm{don}}+\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}}
+\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}}=\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\tag{42}
\]
No selector-tail probability enters (42), so coverage is exact and finite-sample for every compatible envelope, including \(B=D^2\).

For expected length, \texttt{lem:full-data-local-polynomial-control} gives on every successful fit
\[
R_{\mathrm{hist}}
\le B\left\{\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{hist}})c_G^{-1}
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{evt}}
=B\left\{\frac12\log(2/\alpha_{\mathrm{evt}})
R_{\mathrm{tr}}\right\}^{1/2}.
\tag{43}
\]
The support of \(K\) and the same deterministic weight bound give
\[
A_L\le C\sum_s\pi_sh_s^\lambda.
\]
Apply \texttt{lem:geometric-mixing-selector-control} with exponent \(\lambda\), conditionally on the projected donor center, and use Cauchy--Schwarz across the fixed cohorts.  Then
\[
\sup_P\mathbb E_P[A_L\mathbf1_{\mathcal G}\mid E_0]
\le C\{R_{\mathrm{sm}}^{1/2}
+R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}^{1/2}+N^{-\lambda/2}\}
\le CR_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{44}
\]
Since \(D,B,\alpha\) are fixed, (38) implies \(q_N\le C\), and hence
\[
A_{\mathrm{don}}\le CN^{-\kappa/2}=CR_{\mathrm{don}}^{1/2}.
\tag{45}
\]
The selector lemma gives \(P_P(\mathcal G^c\mid E_0)\le CR_{\star,\beta}\) along the asserted arrays.  The fallback length is at most \(2B\), eventually \(R_{\star,\beta}\le R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\), and \(\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\le2H_\alpha\) on \(\mathcal G\).  Equations (43)--(45) therefore prove, for either compatible regime with its independently quantified upper constant,
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}^{\dagger}(\lambda)}
\mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_\alpha)\mid E_0]
\le C_\alpha^{\mathrm{up}}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}.
\tag{46}
\]

For the strict-slack lower bound, choose the fixed perturbation constants in the four channels of \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding} so that every affinity \(A_q\) exceeds \(2\alpha+a_0\) for some fixed \(a_0>0\).  For the three Kullback--Leibler-controlled channels this follows by taking their perturbations sufficiently small in (15); in the donor channel the permissible constants may depend on \(B-D^2\).  For spacing it follows by decreasing the rare-block constant.  Let \(I\) be finite-sample conditionally honest, let \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) be a channel pair's targets, and let \(\mu_q=P_{0,q}\wedge P_{1,q}\) be the conditional overlap measure.  Uniform conditional honesty gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_q\{\theta_0,\theta_1\in I\}
&\ge\mu_q(\Omega)
-P_{0,q}\{\theta_0\notin I\mid E_0\}
-P_{1,q}\{\theta_1\notin I\mid E_0\}\\
&\ge A_q-2\alpha\ge a_0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{47}
\]
On this event, \(\operatorname{length}(I)\ge|\theta_1-\theta_0|\).  Consequently
\[
\max_{\ell\in\{0,1\}}
\mathbb E_{P_{\ell,q}}[\operatorname{length}(I)\mid E_0]
\ge a_0|\theta_1-\theta_0|
\ge c_\alpha R_q^{1/2}.
\tag{48}
\]
Maximizing (48) over all four channels gives the strict-slack lower bound \(c_{\alpha,>}R_{\star,\beta}^{1/2}\).  At \(B=D^2\), apply the same argument only to the treated, smoothing, and spacing pairs supplied at the boundary by \texttt{lem:joint-law-embedding}; maximizing over those three channels gives
\[
c_{\alpha,=}\{R_{\mathrm{tr}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sm}}\vee R_{\mathrm{sp},\beta}\}^{1/2},
\]
without a donor-channel claim.  If an interval sequence is only uniformly asymptotically conditionally honest, then for each \(\epsilon>0\) both noncoverage probabilities are eventually at most \(\alpha+\epsilon\).  Choosing \(\epsilon<a_0/4\) replaces the final bound in (47) by at least \(a_0/2\), proving the same rates.  Equations (42), (46), and (48), with the stated case split, establish every assertion.
